issues.legal_issue: Mining operations assessed as unsuitable for continuation, or falling within designated closure classes, must be discontinued.
material_facts: The petitions concerned limestone quarrying and the Court had received reports from a court-appointed committee and a government working group.
The Court accepted the reports’ assessments that some quarries were unsuitable for continued mining and directed their closure.

The Court also directed closure of other quarries assigned to a designated closure class, subject to specified exceptions, and closed quarries in a sensitive area despite their placement in an intermediate class.
issues.conclusion: The Court directed that the quarries it identified as unsuitable or within the applicable closure classes be closed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court accepted the findings and reasons in the Bhargav Committee and Working Group reports. It relied on those assessments to distinguish quarries suitable for continued operation from those that should be closed; no earlier cases were cited for this determination.

predicates.mining_writ_proceeding: A court considered a public-interest proceeding concerning the operation of mines or quarries.
predicates.joint_reports_find_mining_unsuitable: Inspection reports assessing the mine concluded that it was unsuitable for continued operation.
predicates.mine_falls_in_closure_class_without_revi: The mine was assigned to a class designated for closure and was not among the cases reserved for further review.
predicates.mine_is_in_sensitive_area_requiring_clos: The mine was situated in an area for which the court directed closure even though its general classification would otherwise permit further consideration.

issues.definition: When a mining proceeding concerns a mine that the reports find unsuitable, that falls within a closure class without an applicable review exception, or that is in an area requiring closure, the mine's operations must be closed.

issues.legal_issue: A mine whose suitability for continued operation requires further assessment should not be finally permitted to operate or permanently closed until a proposed operating scheme has been reviewed.
material_facts: The reports differed on whether quarries in an intermediate class should continue operating.
The Court did not adopt the more restrictive recommendation for all such quarries; it allowed their lessees to submit schemes for review by a high-powered committee.

The Court directed further review for certain quarries in an intermediate class and for otherwise suitable quarries within an urban area, and gave the same review direction to specified exceptions from a broader closure direction.
issues.conclusion: The Court deferred the final decision on continued operation or permanent closure of the identified quarries pending review of proposed schemes, after which operation could be allowed subject to conditions.
issues.legal_principle: Where the committee assessments did not justify either unconditional continuation or immediate permanent closure, the Court provided for further scheme-based examination and possible conditions. The Court relied on the Bhargav Committee and Working Group reports and cited no earlier cases for this determination.

predicates.mining_writ_proceeding: A court considered a public-interest proceeding concerning the operation of mines or quarries.
predicates.mine_has_intermediate_suitability_assess: The mine was assessed in a way that left its suitability for continued operation unresolved or disputed.
predicates.suitable_mine_is_within_urban_area: A mine otherwise assessed as suitable for operation was located within an urban area to which further review was directed.
predicates.mine_is_exception_reserved_for_scheme_re: A mine excluded from a general closure direction was instead designated for review of a proposed operating scheme.

issues.definition: When a mining proceeding concerns a mine with an unresolved suitability assessment, a suitable mine within an urban area, or an exception reserved for scheme review, the final decision on operation or permanent closure must await review of a proposed scheme.

issues.legal_issue: A mine assessed as suitable for continued operation and located outside an urban area may operate subject to compliance with applicable mining and safety requirements.
material_facts: The Bhargav Committee and Working Group both assessed the relevant class of quarries as suitable for continued mining.
The Court permitted the quarries in that class that were outside the urban limits to operate subject to applicable mining, safety, and other regulatory requirements.
issues.conclusion: The Court allowed the identified suitable quarries outside the urban area to operate, subject to compliance with applicable requirements.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on the concordant suitability assessments in the Bhargav Committee and Working Group reports and conditioned continued operation on compliance with the Mines Act 1952, the Metalliferous Mines Regulations 1961, and other relevant statutes, rules, and regulations. No earlier cases were cited.

predicates.mining_writ_proceeding: A court considered a public-interest proceeding concerning the operation of mines or quarries.
predicates.reports_assess_mine_suitable: The relevant inspection assessments concluded that the mine was suitable for continued operation.
predicates.mine_is_outside_urban_area: The mine was located outside the relevant urban limits.

issues.definition: When a mining proceeding concerns a mine assessed as suitable and located outside an urban area, the mine may operate subject to applicable requirements.

issues.legal_issue: Authorities granting mineral leases must balance industrial development against risks to human welfare and ecological conditions and provide adequate safeguards.
material_facts: The Court observed that mineral exploitation can support industrial and economic development.

It also found that haphazard or reckless mining can cause loss of life and property, impair basic amenities such as water supply, harm livelihoods and living conditions, and disturb ecological balance.
The Court stated that adequate safeguards at the time of granting leases could have avoided the need to close many mines and some resulting hardship.
issues.conclusion: Authorities granting mining leases should consider the effects of mining on people and the environment and provide adequate safeguards.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the principle that industrial development and conservation must be reconciled by balancing economic benefits against harm to human welfare and ecological conditions. It cited no statutory provision or earlier case for this general observation.

predicates.mineral_lease_grant_decision: An appropriate authority was considering whether to grant a lease for mineral exploitation.
predicates.mining_poses_material_human_or_ecologica: The contemplated mining could materially threaten human life, property, basic amenities, livelihoods, living conditions, or ecological balance.

issues.definition: When a lease authority considers mineral exploitation that poses material risks to people or ecological conditions, it must consider those risks and provide adequate safeguards.
